Help.Connect: Choose a device source in Settings and save it, then discover and connect devices in the workspace. Changing the source stops the session and disconnects existing devices.
Help.Discovery: Bluetooth requires Windows 10 (2004) or later. Turn on the device, bring it closer, disconnect other control apps, and scan again. Local simulation sends no Bluetooth commands.
Help.Linked: Choose a type above the left list and add waveform, touch, audio, restraint, exercise or sleep-deprivation instances. Devices appear inside their assigned mode. A device belongs to one mode even while stopped; remove it before reassigning. Routing is locked while starting, running or paused. Bluetooth connection and mode assignment are separate actions. Save modes to keep each instance’s parameters and local playlist.
Help.LiveWave: Use the workspace waveform picker to change waves during a session. The new wave starts from its beginning while devices, strength, and the session timer are preserved.
Help.Output: A mode can start with both A/B channels at 0%, then change strength while running. Every target uses the mode’s output limit. Single-channel devices ignore channel B. Shared A/B waveforms can use a half-cycle offset.
Help.Readings: Sent strength is the command percentage after limits are applied, not a measured current. The waveform preview shows the configured curve, not a physical device measurement.
Help.StopBehavior: Connecting starts with output off. Stop or timer expiry affects only that mode. Changing pages, viewed devices or selected modes keeps other modes running. Stop all, Esc, changing the device source and closing the app stop every mode. Saved modes never start automatically.
Help.Disconnection: A disconnect or output fault stops the mode that owns the device, including its other targets. Other modes keep running. Software cannot confirm physical output after a device loses its connection.
Help.Storage: Statistics, global settings, mode presets, custom waveforms and sessions are separate local files. Modes save parameters and target device IDs, without reconnecting or starting output on launch. Session logs roll at 128 KiB and keep one old file; cumulative statistics remain. Development versions reset older data formats.
Help.Timer: Enable the timer and drag the duration slider; arrow keys adjust by one second. Starting a session replaces the slider with shrinking progress and a countdown. With the timer off, the session runs until you stop it.
Help.TimerLimit: Set the slider maximum under Settings → Maximum timer duration, from 1–120 minutes. Lowering it shortens all mode durations that exceed it. Each mode’s timer is locked while starting or running; the global maximum is locked while any mode is starting or running.
Help.Waves: Built-in waveforms cannot be deleted or overwritten; copy one to edit it. Custom waveforms support JSON import and export. Electrical devices reject motor waveforms.
History.Help: Sessions are stored in compact JSON Lines. Files roll at 128 KiB; one previous file is kept.
Settings.AppearanceHelp: Theme and accent color follow system settings and update automatically on supported platforms.
Settings.BluetoothHelp: Scan and connect supported Bluetooth devices. Windows uses native GATT; other desktop platforms require a Bluetooth adapter implementation.

Help.Playback: Waveform modes have A/B waveform selection and a custom ordered playlist. Add, remove or reorder entries while stopped. Sequential and random playback use only this list and start at its first entry; random playback avoids consecutive repeats when possible. Repeat and once use the selected A/B waveforms. Touch modes use the touch pad and release behavior instead.
Help.StrengthProgram: Expand Automatic strength and temporary boost to choose fixed, random, or step increases. Zero-strength channels stay at zero; all changes respect the mode’s output limit. A step target below the base strength does not lower it. Hold the boost to add strength, release to restore it, or reset the automatic increase. Pause zeros this mode’s output and freezes its active time until resumed.
Help.DeviceFeatures: Each mode’s advanced controls include gentle mode and electrode-status visibility. Gentle mode uses lower protocol intensity at the same displayed percentage. Hiding contact status only affects the display. Select a physical device to read firmware and light status. Compatible confirmed V2 firmware can switch its light while the device is idle; missing or invalid replies keep the action unavailable.
Help.Touch: Create a touch mode, assign compatible devices and start. Hold and drag: horizontal controls frequency (1–100), vertical controls pulse width or vibration amplitude (0–100). ABC controls set the base strength. On release choose output off, recorded loop or hold. Recordings hold up to 256 frames sampled every 100 ms. Stop and name a recording of at least two frames to save it as a custom waveform in the target family.

Audio.LocalHelp: Audio is processed locally. Microphone and system audio are neither recorded nor uploaded.
Audio.SystemHelp: Captures the default playback device on Windows. Microphone and local-file input also support macOS and Linux.
Audio.FileHelp: WAV, MP3 or FLAC; up to 100 MiB. Media playback pauses and stops with this mode.
Input.MotionHelp: Uses each target device’s accelerometer. Missing or stale data (over 2 seconds) produces zero output. Movement counts represent detected angle changes, not calibrated walking steps.
Restraint.Help: The first valid reading sets the baseline. Output is zero inside the safe angle; beyond it, strength rises across the ramp angle up to the configured base strength. Each target has its own runtime baseline.
Restraint.Recalibrate: Set the current angle as baseline
Exercise.Help: Movement above the sensitivity threshold resets the waiting interval. Inactivity triggers a timed output, followed by another waiting interval. Higher sensitivity detects smaller angle changes. The timer and manual stop remain available.
Exercise.MovementGoal: Stop when all targets reach the movement goal
Sleep.Help: Wait, output for the configured duration, then repeat. Random mode draws timing, strength ratios and A/B waveforms from local settings. Movement resets only the waiting phase; pause, stop and the session timer always apply.
Sleep.StrengthRange: Random strength ratio (% of current strength): min / max
Playlist.SleepHelp: Each random cycle independently chooses A/B waveforms from this local pool. Up to 100 different waveforms. Edit while stopped; save modes to keep the pool.

Help.AudioControl: Choose a local WAV/MP3/FLAC file, the default microphone, or Windows system playback. Inputs open only when you start or explicitly calibrate. Volume/rhythm mapping and sensitivity control the response; ambient calibration samples 2 seconds without starting device output. Speaker volume affects file playback only. Silence, missing or stale audio data, and media completion produce zero output while input stays open; fresh frames resume the response. Stop or an enabled session timer releases input. Actual input device faults stop only this mode. Audio is processed locally and live capture is never saved.
Help.Restraint: The first valid sensor sample establishes each target’s baseline. The safe angle produces zero output; the ramp angle determines how quickly output reaches the current strength. Recalibrate sets a new baseline while running. Missing or stale data over 2 seconds produces zero output. The simulation slider is available only with simulated devices.
Help.Exercise: Movement resets the inactivity interval while waiting. After inactivity, output runs for the chosen duration, then the next wait begins. Sensitivity controls the angle-change threshold. The optional movement goal completes when all targets reach it; counts represent detected movement, not calibrated steps. The session timer and manual stop always apply.
Help.Sleep: Fixed mode repeats a waiting interval and timed output. Random mode chooses intervals, durations, strength ratios and A/B waveforms from local settings and the local pool. Activity-reset mode restarts the wait when device motion is detected; it requires fresh sensor input. Pause freezes active time. A stalled/suspended app restarts the wait instead of replaying a missed output.
Error.WaveDeviceMismatch: A waveform is incompatible with an assigned device. Choose a compatible waveform or edit the local playlist.
Error.ModeDeviceMismatch: This mode is incompatible with an assigned device. Pumps require pump mode; motion modes require a motion-capable device.
Error.SensorOnly: Input devices cannot be assigned as output targets.
Error.PawFirmware: Paw V1.0 is unsupported; upgrade to V1.1 firmware.
Pump.Help: Select peristaltic direction and the water pump switch, then start. Changes apply during playback. Pause and stop turn both pumps off. Commands renew a one-second firmware duration while running; the protocol has no flow percentage setting. Pressure readings use raw protocol values because the manufacturer does not specify a unit.
Dg.BalanceHelp: Saved with this mode. Applied on start with the mode’s output limit; edit while stopped. The V3 hardware limit is set to zero on stop and connection.
Telemetry.Title: Device readings
Help.Hardware: YOKONEX electrical, vibration and pump devices; DG-LAB Coyote V2/V3 and Opossum. Paw V1.1 and Civet connect as input devices. Old Paw V1.0 firmware needs an upgrade. Choose pump control for pumps. Motion modes require YOKONEX electrical motion data. All settings belong to the mode, and each output device can belong to only one mode.
Help.HardwareWaves: YOKONEX and DG-LAB native electrical waveforms use different parameters and cannot be mixed. Generated waves and sliding/audio controls can drive either family. The DG-LAB defaults are the manufacturer’s public Breathing/Tide examples. Motor devices accept nonnegative motor values only; directional waves are unavailable on these protocols. Channel C follows channel A’s waveform and, in audio mode, the left input.
Help.Sensors: Paw shows button, motion and external-voltage data; Civet shows pressure in kPa and supports pressure zeroing. Input devices do not appear as output targets. Sensor-to-mode rules and Opossum screen synchronization are not implemented. Readings include their last update time.
